name: HeyGen Remote MCP
tagline: Hosted MCP for avatar videos, lipsync, and 175-language video translation.
description: HeyGen's official hosted MCP endpoint lets agents create and manage HeyGen videos with no local install and no API key — auth is a one-time OAuth flow tied to your HeyGen account. The published tool surface spans Video Agent one-prompt and multi-turn generation, video translation with lip-sync (175+ languages), lipsync jobs, avatar groups and looks, templates, voice design and cloning, music and SFX search, AI clipping of long footage, filler-word removal, brand kits and glossaries, and batches of up to 100 videos, translations, or lipsyncs per request.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http heygen https://mcp.heygen.com/mcp/v1/

auth.key_url: One-time browser OAuth tied to your HeyGen account

notes: Endpoint, OAuth flow and plan terms re-confirmed against HeyGen's own MCP docs on 2026-09-08: unchanged, available on all HeyGen plans, generation consumes plan credits, no API key. There is still no local option: HeyGen's own heygen-com/heygen-mcp 404s, and the community fork this entry used to recommend (sbroenne/heygen-mcp) has 404'd too — its PyPI package heygen-mcp-sbroenne is still installable but frozen at 0.3.1 from 2026-01-31 with its source gone, so treat it as abandoned. The hosted remote is the only maintained route. HeyGen's official Agent Skills (heygen-com/skills) remain active — 429 stars, still pushed 2026-07-14, so the skills repo has gained attention but no commits in nearly two months.

name: Hedra MCP Server
tagline: Character-3 talking-avatar video, TTS, and image generation through Hedra's API.
description: Node MCP server for Hedra's generation API: lip-synced character video from an image plus audio (Character-3), text-to-speech, image generation, and asset/credit management. Its README also advertises third-party models reachable through Hedra Studio, though that list dates from the server's only release and has since drifted from Hedra's own roster.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add hedra -e HEDRA_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx -y mcp-server-hedra

notes: No longer the only way in: Hedra shipped an official hosted MCP on 2026-08-31 at mcp.hedra.com, listed here as `hedra-official`, and it is the better default — OAuth instead of a pasted key, and the current model roster instead of a frozen one. Reach for this community server only when you want named Character-3 tools driven by a plain API key, which the official endpoint does not document. Re-checked 2026-09-09 and nothing here has moved: npm mcp-server-hedra is still the 1.0.0 published 2026-02-08, the repo has had no push since the same day, MIT, Node 18+, 2 stars. Drifts to expect against its README: the key page is hedra.com/develop/api-keys (the README's /api-profile link is stale), and the third-party model list has aged badly — Hedra's platform now fronts Seedance 2.5, MiniMax Hailuo 2.3, Kling 2.6 Pro and Nano Banana Pro, while Sora 2 leaves OpenAI's API on 2026-09-24. Character-3 itself is alive and still on Hedra's model page. The API bills against the same Studio credit balance as the app and needs a paid subscription.

name: Tavus MCP
tagline: Phoenix replicas, persona videos, lipsync, and conversational AI via the Tavus API.
description: Comprehensive community MCP server exposing 25 tools across the full Tavus API: Phoenix replica (digital twin) training, persona management, video generation, real-time conversational video (CVI), lipsync, and speech synthesis. Tavus now ships a first-party MCP too, but it covers only conversational-agent configuration — for replica training, video generation and lipsync this is still the only MCP that reaches them.

install.stdio_command: Build from source: clone rakeshdavid/Tavus-MCP, npm install && npm run build, then run node build/index.js with TAVUS_API_KEY. Smithery is the documented alternative: npx -y @smithery/cli install @rakeshdavid/tavus-mcp --client claude

notes: The landscape changed on 2026-08-31 and the answer did not. Tavus now has an official MCP — hosted at https://mcp.tavus.io/mcp (`claude mcp add -s user --transport http tavus https://mcp.tavus.io/mcp`, browser OAuth, no key in your config) or locally via `uvx --from 'tavus-cli[daily]' tavus-mcp` from PyPI tavus-cli 0.4.3. It is not a substitute: all 72 of its tools configure PALs — prompts, objectives, guardrails, knowledge, tool wiring, chat-mode testing — and Tavus's own tools reference lists no replica training, no video generation and no lipsync. That is a conversational-agent product, which is why it is not listed here separately and this server still is. What you are living with, re-confirmed 2026-09-09: the README's npm package (tavus-mcp) is still not on npm — the registry 404s — so install from source or via Smithery; the repo has had no commit since 2025-07-09 and holds 2 stars, so treat it as unmaintained rather than quiet; it is built on an old MCP SDK version. Tavus free developer plan: ~25 min conversational video + 5 min generation.

name: D-ID MCP Server
tagline: D-ID's hosted MCP connecting agents to the D-ID API and docs for avatar video.
description: D-ID hosts an official remote MCP server on its developer docs that lets MCP clients interact with the D-ID API and its documentation for talking-avatar and Agents workflows. D-ID also publishes llms.txt for agent consumption.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http d-id https://docs.d-id.com/mcp

auth.key_url: https://docs.d-id.com/docs/api-keys (D-ID Studio; credits required for API calls)

notes: Docs-platform-hosted (ReadMe-powered) remote MCP; endpoint and setup text re-confirmed unchanged on 2026-09-09, and the exact tool list is still not published openly — D-ID describes the surface only as API access, docs search, live account data and code generation. Auth is whatever your client can send: D-ID's own guidance is that you pass API credentials as headers or query parameters through the MCP client, so there is no OAuth flow and no standard env var. Manage expectations about what a docs-platform MCP is — it is closer to a documentation copilot with API reach than a purpose-built generation server, and nothing about the tool surface is contractual. Landscape note: Synthesia still has no official MCP (only marginal community wrappers and generic Zapier/viaSocket gateways).

name: Sync MCP Server
tagline: Official Sync MCP for lipsync generation, voice cloning, and TTS on existing footage.
description: Sync's own MCP server wraps the sync.so API: take a video plus an audio track and regenerate the performer's mouth to match, with cost estimation before you spend, asset and project management, voice cloning, and TTS. Unlike avatar platforms that synthesize a presenter, this retimes lips on footage you already shot — the practical tool for dub passes, ADR fixes, and localized versions that keep the original take. Tools are generated from the Sync OpenAPI spec at startup, so new endpoints appear without a server update.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add sync -- npx -y @sync.so/mcp-server --api-key YOUR_API_KEY

notes: Official and MIT, and every install field above re-checked unchanged: the hosted endpoint takes OAuth in Claude web (no key needed), while stdio needs SYNC_API_KEY — or omit it and the server runs a device-auth flow, caching a token at ~/.config/sync/mcp-credentials.json. Node 18+. Pricing is the same on re-check — $5/month Hobbyist through $249/month Scale, per-second generation charges of roughly $0.04–0.05 on every tier, and caps on clip length (1 min at the bottom, 30 min at the top), concurrent jobs and voice clones — so call generate_estimate-cost before long renders; the pricing page pitches a free trial but lists no free plan. Models named there are still Lipsync-2-Pro, Sync-3 and React-1; ask models_get rather than assuming. Watch the surface mismatch: the repo README documents voices, tts and projects tools, but Sync's public API reference only covers generations, assets, models, estimate, batch and healthcheck — tools are generated from the live OpenAPI spec at startup, so read tools/list instead of trusting either list. The repo woke up (last pushed 7 Sep 2026, adding session and upload limits to the HTTP transport) but is still a 1-star project, and npm @sync.so/mcp-server sits at 0.1.4 from 16 Mar 2026 — tolerable only because the tool surface comes from the spec, not the package. Ethics and rights: relighting someone's mouth to say new words needs the performer's consent, and many jurisdictions and union agreements now require it explicitly.

name: VEED Fabric MCP
tagline: VEED's hosted MCP for talking-head video: pick a character, pick a voice, send a script.
description: VEED's official remote MCP drives Fabric, its talking-head engine: agents browse 24+ stock characters and multi-language voices, price a render before committing, submit a script, then poll for the finished MP4. It is deliberately one job rather than an editing suite — the piece a film pipeline reaches for when a scene needs a presenter, a spokesperson insert, or a localized to-camera read without booking a shoot. Credit balance and workspace tools are exposed too, so an agent can check what a batch will cost before it spends.

auth.key_url: OAuth 2.0 against a VEED account — in Claude, add VEED Fabric from Settings › Connectors

notes: Endpoint verified alive on 17 Aug 2026 (401 unauthenticated), Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0. Seven tools, and that is the whole surface: stock characters only — nothing in the documented toolset uploads your own plate or clones a voice, so this does not replace Sync or Hedra for footage you shot. Costs roughly 8 credits per second of output, billed against AI Playground credits that come with paid VEED plans or are bought separately, so call confirm_fabric_video first; create_fabric_video is async and returns a job id you poll with get_generation_status. VEED publishes no CLI one-liner — the documented Claude path is the connector directory at claude.ai, and the command shown here is the generic Streamable HTTP form. The linked repo is documentation plus an Agent Skill, not the server: the server is closed-source and hosted, the repo has ~6 stars, and it was last pushed 1 Aug 2026, so judge maintenance by VEED the product rather than by repo activity.

name: Apatero Studio MCP
tagline: Studio MCP for talking avatars, locked recurring characters, and batched output.
description: Apatero Studio is a hosted generation service whose MCP is organised around persistence rather than one-off clips: Souls are named characters you create once and then generate against, so the same face and wardrobe survive across images, video and talking-avatar takes. Beyond the character tools it covers plain image and video generation, remixes, brand-locked output, short stories, and a batching pipeline that fills a week of posts from one brief. For a filmmaker the relevant slice is narrow but real — a reusable synthetic performer with a consistent look, plus talking-head coverage of it, without running a model locally.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add apatero -- npx apatero-mcp
install.stdio_command: npx apatero-mcp (or uvx apatero-studio-mcp); for headless use add --env APATERO_API_KEY=ap_live_your_key

auth.key_url: https://apatero.ai/mcp — browser OAuth by default, or an ap_live_ API key for headless clients

notes: Endpoint verified alive 21 Sep 2026: an unauthenticated initialize returns 401 asking for 'Authorization: Bearer <ap_live_ key or OAuth access token>' with protected-resource metadata pointing at api.apatero.ai. Tools were not run — there is no anonymous path. Be careful copying install commands for this one from search results or AI summaries: a `claude mcp add --transport http apatero ... --header` form circulates widely and does not appear anywhere on the vendor's own page, which documents only the connector UI for the remote and npx/uvx/brew for local. Both packages exist but each has shipped exactly one version — npm apatero-mcp 0.2.0 and PyPI apatero-studio-mcp 0.2.0, both 10 Jul 2026 — and the repository URL in the PyPI metadata, github.com/Apatero-Org/Monorepo, 404s, so there is no readable source and no public commit history to judge. The vendor page headlines '20 tools' while 24 apatero_ names appear on it, several of them documentation helpers rather than studio tools; treat live tools/list as the count. Positioning is social-first — the Insta Dump and influencer pipeline are aimed at feed content, not narrative coverage — so for shot-matched performance work on footage you actually shot, hedra-official, sync-labs or tavus remain the stronger picks. Generation spends Apatero account credits at app rates with no MCP markup; apatero_credit_balance reports the remainder in chat.
